title: The Incident
briefing: Allied security services have disrupted a biological plot at the acquisition stage, and AI assistance is alleged. Nothing was released. The story is public, ministers want a response today, and the advice in the room is not agreed.

forecast.question: Chance of a further AI-assisted biological plot in an allied country before the end of 2032.

shah.stance: The plot failed at acquisition, which is where existing controls sit. One case does not tell us the model mattered.

memory.line: We funded the uplift studies in 2028 so that we would not have to guess today. Read the result before you read the headlines.

harcourt.stance: They got as far as acquisition. Screen every synthesis order, by law, now.

memory.line: In 2028 I asked for mandatory synthesis screening. It was the one measure that works whichever model is used.

chen.stance: Unilateral screening moves orders abroad and protects nobody. If we act, act with the allies who were targeted.

okafor.stance: The public will accept firm controls on synthesis. They will not accept being told nothing has changed.

choices.text: Conventional counter-terrorism response under existing powers.
choices.headline: Government treats the plot as a counter-terrorism matter under existing powers.

choices.text: Emergency synthesis screening for UK providers and customers.
choices.headline: Emergency legislation makes synthesis screening mandatory across the UK.

onFailure.headline: Allies decline a joint synthesis-control regime; the UK proposal is shelved.

choices.headline: The UK and its allies agree common controls on synthesis orders.
The government's own incident-response model supports the allied investigation; ministers can say what the AI did and did not contribute.

evidencePanel.known: A 2024 red-team study found models of that generation did not measurably raise attack-planning risk. Research on focusing events shows that regulation tends to follow disasters rather than precede them.
evidencePanel.unknown: How much the AI assistance mattered to this plot, compared with everything else the plotters needed.
evidencePanel.whyItMatters: Restriction is cheapest after the harm and most expensive when it would have prevented it.

sources.label: RAND, The Operational Risks of AI in Large-Scale Biological Attacks (2024)
Birkland, Focusing Events, Mobilization, and Agenda Setting (1998)
